thread.title: East Lyme, the two-time defending CT champion, wins Section 3 Little League championship - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: East Lyme, the two-time defending CT champion, wins Section 3 Little League championship - NewsBreak

title: East Lyme, the two-time defending CT champion, wins Section 3 Little League championship - NewsBreak
text:
GUILFORD — There was a good chance that Ben Lubeski wouldn’t pitch this season for the East Lyme Little League baseball majors (10-12) team. Lubeski was shut down after he suffered a fracture in the growth plate in his right elbow during his first game of the season. He was allowed to hit once he returned but pitching was out of the question, as was his ability to throw at all for his team. Lubeski sure didn’t look like a player who had been injured earlier in the year on Wednesday night. He made quick work of Guilford, needing a little over an hour to pitch a one-hitter with six strikeouts to help two-time defending state champion East Lyme beat Guilford, 4-1, to win the state Section 3 championship at Adams Middle School. “I was hoping in Little League (tournament play) that I might be able to pitch,” Lubeski said. “It feels great to be back on the mound.” East Lyme moves on to the State Final Four and will play the Section 4 champion Tolland on Monday at North Haven. “Benny wasn’t supposed to pitch this year, to be honest,” East Lyme head coach Dan Mason said. “He did physical therapy (and) he got cleared. We limited to like 30 pitches, and then it became 50 pitches. “As you saw tonight, he just pounds the strike zone. And we always tell him, ‘You have a really good defense behind you. Trust your defense.’” Lubeski’s first inning was a harbinger for the rest of the game as he needed just four pitches to retire Guilford’s first three batters. “(I) just pounded the strike zone,” Lubeski said. “Curve ball, curve ball, curve ball, curve ball.” Lubeski walked just one and didn’t give up an earned run. He threw just 68 pitches, 44 for strikes. Andrew Messier and Evan Stutt each went 2-for-3 and scored for East Lyme, while Colton Buhler and Bryce Mason both singled and scored. Zac Bodin singled and scored on John Rubinstein’s sacrifice fly for Guilford, the District 4 champion. “It’s amazing, you know,” Guilford head coach Chris Frey said. “I tell them. … ‘This is something that you will talk about for the rest of your life. These are lifelong friendships, the memories that we’ve had.’ “It’s always hard to end with a loss but you’ve got to look back at all the fun we had and the hard work (they) put into it. And, you know, we put a (district) banner up.” Kashton Kaczor singled to score Stutt with two outs in the East Lyme first. Mason scored on a throwing error in the bottom of the second. Messier scored on a throwing error with no outs in the East Lyme fourth. Lubeski followed with a sacrifice fly to score Buhler and push East Lyme ahead 4-0. Bodin scored on John Rubinstein’s sacrifice fly in the fifth inning for Guilford. Tommy Armstrong, Brady Donovan, Panagioti Faraone, Jack Hayes, Nico Russo, Gary Swanson round out East Lyme’s lineup. “We’re making a run for the state championship for a third time,” Dan Mason said. “We’ve been very fortunate and we’ve got a strong program. (There are) high expectations.” Ben Lubeski , East Lyme. He faced 21 batters, needed just 68 pitches — and one hour and eight minutes — to pitch a one-hitter with six strikeouts. (At Adams Middle School, Guilford) Guilford 000 010—1 1 2
